title: Design Patterns Examples
description: Small Design Patterns examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Patterns solve repeated problems
examples.description: A pattern gives a name to a useful design idea. Before choosing one, describe the job the code must do.
examples.code:
const job = { input: 3, action: n => n * 2 };
console.log(job.action(job.input));

examples.title: Factory functions
examples.description: A factory makes objects. It keeps object creation in one place so callers do not repeat the setup.
examples.code:
function makeBook(title) { return { title, borrowed: false }; }
console.log(makeBook("Moon").borrowed);

examples.title: Strategy functions
examples.description: A strategy is a swappable way to do a job. Pass a function when the rule may change.

examples.title: Observer notifications
examples.description: An observer listens for a change. The subject tells its listeners when something happens.

examples.title: Adapters translate interfaces
examples.description: An adapter changes one form of input or output into another. It lets two parts work together without changing both.

examples.title: Decorators add behaviour
examples.description: A decorator wraps a function with extra behaviour. The original function can stay focused on its job.

examples.title: Facades offer a small doorway
examples.description: A facade gives callers a simple way to use several parts. It hides the order of small steps behind one clear action.

examples.title: Commands store actions
examples.description: A command packages an action so it can be saved in a queue and run later.

examples.title: State changes allowed behaviour
examples.description: State describes the current condition of an object. Different states can allow different actions.

examples.title: Builders collect choices
examples.description: A builder collects choices before producing a result. It helps when creation has several optional parts.

examples.title: Shared state needs care
examples.description: A single shared object can be convenient, but every caller sees its changes. This makes hidden links between features.

examples.title: Choose the smallest useful design
examples.description: Compare designs by clarity and the changes you expect. A function, a plain object or a pattern can each be the right choice.
examples.code:
const discounts = { none: n => n, half: n => n / 2 };
console.log(discounts.half(12));
